about: Proposed unified B4 permission model. Each right has one polarity for macOS and both Linux labs. This file is a proposal. The checker scores platforms against it. It does not edit confine.sb, lab/linux-confine, or lab/fail-closed-linux.
role: proposed unified baseline, not a grant and not applied
fail_closed: Where a polarity is unsure, this file proposes the tighter side and sets open_decision so Sash and Anders decide.

rights.title: exec the bound provider binary
rights.rationale: Every side already grants execute of the one bound provider binary and refuses any other file. The unified model keeps that allow.

rights.title: read and write under STORAGE_ROOT
rights.rationale: The approved storage right is the eight-right mask on STORAGE_ROOT (0x41be). macOS uses the subpath write rule. Both Linux labs grant the same eight bits and omit ioctl, refer, and special-file create.

rights.title: literal read of STORAGE_PARENT only
rights.rationale: STORAGE_PARENT is its own right here, split out of C8 storage. Landlock cannot name a directory alone: a path rule on the host parent covers siblings. Linux is already the tighter side (missing on did/model; wallet on #296 remounts a private parent). Fail-closed proposes deny of a host-parent grant. C8 still bundles the Seatbelt literal under storage, and macOS init has F-cc1-rm-parent, so this stays an open decision. The keep-the-right path is the #296 wallet remount on every provider, not a host-parent Landlock rule.

change.macos: drop (allow file-read* (literal (param "STORAGE_PARENT"))) and split STORAGE_PARENT out of the C8 storage right
change.linux-confine: none if deny is adopted; if the right is kept, extend hide_parent_siblings to did and model
change.fail-closed-linux: none if deny is adopted; if the right is kept, add a private-parent mount

rights.title: startup read of /
rights.rationale: One polarity for `/`. A Landlock rule on `/` grants the whole tree, so both Linux labs add none. That is the tighter side. Seatbelt's literal `/` is a macOS loader pin, not a shared grant Linux can copy. Fail-closed proposes deny as the unified right. Open until a named test shows the macOS loader starts without that pin, or Sash and Anders reclassify it as macOS-loader-only and drop it from the shared model.

change.macos: drop (allow file-read* (literal "/")) and the model file-read-data form

rights.title: startup sysctl-read
rights.rationale: One polarity for sysctl-read. Linux has no sysctl right. #307 names none. #296 admits uname and loader syscalls; that is a loader set, not a shared sysctl grant. Fail-closed proposes deny as the unified right. Open until a named test shows the macOS loader starts without sysctl-read, or the C8 baseline names the Linux loader syscalls as Linux-only and drops the shared right.

rights.title: read outside STORAGE_ROOT
rights.rationale: Every side already refuses a read outside STORAGE_ROOT. The unified model keeps that deny.

rights.title: write outside STORAGE_ROOT
rights.rationale: Every side already refuses a write outside STORAGE_ROOT. The unified model keeps that deny.

rights.title: network sockets
rights.rationale: Providers speak stdin/stdout. macOS denies network*. Both Linux labs deny SYS_socket. The unified model keeps that deny.

rights.title: AF_UNIX socketpair
rights.rationale: macOS counts a Unix-domain pair under network* and denies it. #307 denies SYS_socketpair with no AF_UNIX exception. #296 allows AF_UNIX socketpair for Tokio. Fail-closed keeps the tighter deny. A separate fixer is closing the #296 exception. #296 is the side that changes.

change.linux-confine: drop the AF_UNIX socketpair exception so the provider filter denies the pair

rights.title: exec a file other than PROVIDER_EXECUTABLE
rights.rationale: Every side already grants execute only on the bound binary. The unified model keeps that deny.

rights.title: signal a host process
rights.rationale: A provider must not signal a host pid. macOS has no signal-outbound grant. #296 unshares CLONE_NEWPID, so a host pid cannot be named. #307 unshares only CLONE_NEWUSER and sets LANDLOCK_SCOPE_SIGNAL at ABI 6; that is partial, not a deny. The unified model is deny with a PID namespace carrier. #307 is the side that changes.

change.fail-closed-linux: unshare CLONE_NEWPID so a host pid cannot be named; SCOPE_SIGNAL at ABI 6 is not a substitute

rights.title: device ioctl
rights.rationale: IOCTL_DEV is not in the eight-right storage mask. macOS has no file-ioctl grant. Both Linux labs refuse a start that cannot deny ioctl. The unified model keeps that deny.
